questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: An equiconvex lens of focal length $f$, is cut into four parts as shown in the diagram. The focal length of each part is
questions.solution: For an equiconvex lens, focal length $f = \frac{R}{2(\mu - 1)}$. When cut vertically into two halves, each plano-convex lens has focal length $f' = \frac{R}{\mu - 1} = 2f$. Cutting horizontally does not change the focal length of the parts. Thus, the focal length of each of the four parts is $2f$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Radius of a tube decreases from $2R$ to $R$ in which ideal liquid is flowing at same level. Speed at one end is $2\text{ m/s}$ as shown, find speed $v$ at other end
questions.solution:
By equation of continuity:
$A_1 v_1 = A_2 v_2$
$\pi (2R)^2 \cdot 2 = \pi R^2 \cdot v$
$4 \cdot 2 = v \implies v = 8\text{ m/s}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The dimensional formula of capacitance is
questions.solution:
Energy stored in capacitor $E = \frac{Q^2}{2C} \implies C = \frac{Q^2}{2E}$.
$[C] = \frac{[\text{A}^2\text{T}^2]}{[\text{M L}^2 \text{T}^{-2}]} = [\text{M}^{-1}\text{L}^{-2}\text{T}^{4}\text{A}^{2}]$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A proton is moving with uniform velocity of $2 \times 10^8\text{ m/s}$ in uniform magnetic and electric fields which are perpendicular to each other. If electric field is switched off then proton moves in circular path of radius $1.6 \times 10^{-5}\text{ m}$. Then magnetic field is $B$
questions.solution: $r = \frac{mv}{qB} \implies B = \frac{mv}{qr} = \frac{1.6 \times 10^{-27} \times 2 \times 10^8}{1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times 1.6 \times 10^{-5}} = \frac{5}{4} \times 10^5 = 1.25 \times 10^5\text{ T} \approx 1.2 \times 10^5\text{ T}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A conducting circular ring is moving with a constant velocity in a uniform magnetic field as shown. Identify the correct graph between induced emf vs time
questions.solution: Induced emf $\delta = 2Bv\sqrt{R^2 - x^2}$ which represents an ellipse equation, where $x = R - vt$. Hence the graph is elliptical as given in option (1).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The displacement of a particle moving under the action of a force $\vec{F} = 2\hat{i} + b\hat{j} + \hat{k}$ is $\vec{d} = \hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}$. Find the value of $b$ if the work done by the force is zero.
questions.solution: Work done $= \vec{F} \cdot \vec{d} = (2\hat{i} + b\hat{j} + \hat{k}) \cdot (\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}) = 2 + b + 1 = 3 + b = 0 \implies b = -3$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: In a series LCR circuit the maximum amplitude of current is $I_0$ when the resistance is $R$. What is the maximum amplitude of current if the resistor is replaced by a resistor of resistance $\frac{R}{2}$.
questions.solution:
At resonance, the maximum current amplitude is $I_0 = \frac{\xi_0}{R}$.
When resistance is replaced by $R/2$, $I_0' = \frac{\xi_0}{R/2} = 2 \left(\frac{\xi_0}{R}\right) = 2I_0$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
Statement-I : Fringe width of red light is more than fringe width of violet light.
Statement-II : Fringe width is directly proportional to the wavelength of light used.
Choose the correct option.
options: Statement-I is correct and statement-II is incorrect
Both statement-I and statement-II are correct
Statement-I is incorrect and statement-II is correct
Both statement-I and statement-II are incorrect
questions.solution: Fringe width $\beta = \frac{\lambda D}{d}$, which means $\beta \propto \lambda$. Since wavelength of red light is greater than wavelength of violet light ($\lambda_{\text{red}} > \lambda_{\text{violet}}$), fringe width of red light is greater than that of violet light. Thus, both statements are correct.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: For non-vibrating diatomic gas has adiabatic constant of $\gamma_1$ & for vibrating diatomic gas has adiabatic constant of $\gamma_2$ then
questions.solution:
For non-vibrating diatomic gas, degrees of freedom $f = 5 \implies \gamma_1 = 1 + \frac{2}{5} = 1.4$.
For vibrating diatomic gas, degrees of freedom $f = 7 \implies \gamma_2 = 1 + \frac{2}{7} = 1.28$.
Therefore, $\gamma_1 > \gamma_2$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A force $\vec{F} = (\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 3\hat{k})\text{ N}$ acts on point whose position vector is given as $\vec{r} = (2\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + 7\hat{k})\text{ m}$. Find torque about origin.
questions.solution: Torque $\vec{\tau} = \vec{r} \times \vec{F} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 2 & -3 & 7 \\ 1 & 2 & -3 \end{vmatrix} = \hat{i}(9 - 14) - \hat{j}(-6 - 7) + \hat{k}(4 + 3) = (-5\hat{i} + 13\hat{j} + 7\hat{k})\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The net magnetic field at point O due to the two infinite current carrying wires shown in the figure is
questions.solution: $B_{\text{net}} = \frac{\mu_0 (5\text{ A})}{2\pi (10\text{ cm})} - \frac{\mu_0 (4\text{ A})}{2\pi (4\text{ cm})} = \frac{\mu_0}{2\pi} \left( \frac{5}{0.10} - \frac{4}{0.04} \right) = 2 \times 10^{-7} (50 - 100) = -10^{-5}\text{ T}$. Magnitude is $1 \times 10^{-5}\text{ T}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
Read the statements and select the correct option.
Statement I : A pendulum is taken from Earth to another planet having mass four times and radius double than earth, then time period of pendulum remain same as on earth.
Statement II : The time period of pendulum only depends on the gravity of the planet.
options: Statement I is true but statement II is false.
Statement II is true but statement I is false.
questions.solution: On Earth, $T = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{l}{g}}$. On the other planet, $g' = \frac{G(4M)}{(2R)^2} = g$. Thus $T$ remains unchanged. Statement I is true. Statement II is false because $T$ depends on length $l$ as well as $g$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: For a given logic circuit truth table is given identify the gate G.
questions.solution: From the given truth table, the overall function is $y = \bar{A}\bar{B} + AB = \text{XNOR}$. Thus, the final gate G must be a NOR gate.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Name the logic gate
questions.solution: If both inputs A and B are high, the output Y is high; otherwise Y is low. Hence it is an AND Gate.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Displacement current in capacitor of area $16\text{ cm}^2$ is $6\text{ A}$ at an instant. Find displacement current across area $3.2\text{ cm}^2$
questions.solution:
$i_d = \epsilon_0 \frac{d\Phi_E}{dt} = \epsilon_0 A \frac{dE}{dt} \implies i_d \propto A$.
$i' = \left( \frac{3.2}{16} \right) \times 6\text{ A} = 1.2\text{ A}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: In the RC circuit shown, find $I$.
questions.solution: At steady state, capacitor behaves as an open-circuit. The equivalent resistance of the resistor network is $R_{\text{eq}} = \frac{13}{8}R$. Therefore, $I = \frac{V}{R_{\text{eq}}} = \frac{8V}{13R}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A glass slab of refractive index $\mu_g = 1.44$ is coated with a thin film of refractive index $\mu_f = 2$. The minimum thickness of the film so that maximum transmission of green light of wavelength $\lambda = 5000\text{ \AA}$ (incident normally) takes place is
questions.solution:
For maximum transmission of light incident normally:
$2 \mu_f t = n \lambda$ ($n = 1, 2, 3 \dots$)
$t_{\text{min}} = \frac{\lambda}{2 \mu_f} = \frac{5000 \times 10^{-10}}{2(2)} = 1.25 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m} = 0.125\text{ }\mu\text{m}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: For the electric dipole shown in the figure, the electric field and the electric potential are $E_0, V_0$ at a distance $r$ on the axis. Then what is the electric field and the electric potential at a point on the equatorial plane at a distance $2r$.
questions.solution:
$E_{\text{axis}} = \frac{2kP}{r^3} = E_0$, $V_{\text{axis}} = \frac{kP}{r^2} = V_0$.
On the equatorial plane at distance $2r$:
$E_{\text{equatorial}} = \frac{kP}{(2r)^3} = \frac{kP}{8r^3} = \frac{E_0}{16}$.
$V_{\text{equatorial}} = \frac{kP \cos 90^\circ}{(2r)^2} = 0$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A projectile is fired with speed of $20\text{ m/s}$ at angle of $60^\circ$ with horizontal. The speed at highest point of trajectory is $x\text{ m/s}$ then $x$ is
questions.solution:
Horizontal component of velocity remains constant throughout the flight.
Speed at highest point $v_H = v \cos \theta = 20 \cos 60^\circ = 10\text{ m/s}$.
Thus, $x = 10$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: If equivalent resistance across $AB$ is $\frac{NR}{2}$, find $N$
questions.solution:
By line of symmetry:
$R_{\text{eq}} = \frac{3R}{4} \times 2 = \frac{3R}{2}$.
Comparing with $\frac{NR}{2}$, we get $N = 3$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The reaction of toluene with $\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2/\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2$ followed by $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$ and then $\text{NaHSO}_3$ yields the product:
questions.solution: Toluene reacts with Etard's reagent ($\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2$) followed by hydrolysis to form Benzaldehyde, which then forms a sodium bisulfite addition complex $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{-CH(OH)(SO}_3\text{Na)}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Density of $3\text{ M NaOH}$ is $1.25\text{ g/mL}$. Molality of solution is
questions.solution: Molality $m = \frac{1000 M}{1000 d - M \times M_0} = \frac{3 \times 1000}{1250 - 3 \times 40} = \frac{3000}{1130} = 2.65\text{ m}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Arrange according to CFSE.
(i) $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$
(ii) $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$
(iii) $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]^{2+}$
(iv) $[\text{Co(en)}_3]^{3+}$
questions.solution:
CFSE $\propto$ Charge on central metal ion and Ligand field strength.
Therefore, the correct decreasing order of CFSE is $[\text{Co(en)}_3]^{3+} > [\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]^{3+} > [\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]^{2+} > [\text{Co(NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$, i.e., (iv) > (ii) > (iii) > (i).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
What is correct order of stability of carbocation.
(a) $p\text{-methoxybenzyl carbocation}$
(b) $p\text{-methylbenzyl carbocation}$
(c) $m\text{-methoxybenzyl carbocation}$
(d) $m\text{-methylbenzyl carbocation}$
questions.solution: Stability of carbocation $\propto +M, \text{HC}, +I \propto \frac{1}{-M, -I}$. Thus, $a > c > d > b$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following anion will not undergo disproportionation?
questions.solution: In $\text{ClO}_4^-$, chlorine is in its highest oxidation state (+7) and cannot be oxidized further. Therefore, it cannot undergo disproportionation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Compare dipole moment of
(I) $\text{NF}_3$
(II) $\text{CHCl}_3$
(III) $\text{H}_2\text{S}$
(IV) $\text{HBr}$
questions.solution:
Dipole moments: $\text{CHCl}_3 (1.04\text{ D}) > \text{H}_2\text{S} (0.95\text{ D}) > \text{HBr} (0.79\text{ D}) > \text{NF}_3 (0.230\text{ D})$.
So the order is II > III > IV > I.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Given below are two statements
S-I: Lassaigne test is used for detection of Nitrogen, phosphorous, sulphur and Halogens.
S-II: Lassaigne extract is made with magnesium metal.
options: Both S-I and S-II are correct.
Both S-I and S-II are incorrect.
S-I is correct but S-II is incorrect.
S-I is incorrect but S-II is correct
questions.solution: Lassaigne extract is made using sodium metal, not magnesium metal. Thus S-I is correct and S-II is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which one has two secondary Hydrogen atoms?
questions.solution: In 3-ethyl-2, 2-dimethylpentane, there are 2 secondary hydrogen atoms ($2^\circ\text{H} = 2$).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Secondary butyl cyclohexane when reacts with $\text{Br}_2$ in presence of sunlight produce major product:
questions.solution: Free radical bromination occurs preferentially at the tertiary carbon attached to the cyclohexane ring to give 1-bromo-1-sec-butylcyclohexane as the major product.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: $200\text{ mL}$ of $0.2\text{ M}$ solution of $\text{NaOH}$ is mixed with $400\text{ mL}$ of $0.5\text{ M}$ $\text{NaOH}$ solution. Molarity of mixture is
questions.solution: Molarity of mixture $= \frac{M_1 V_1 + M_2 V_2}{V_1 + V_2} = \frac{0.2 \times 200 + 0.5 \times 400}{200 + 400} = \frac{40 + 200}{600} = 0.4\text{ M}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Correct structure of L-Glyceraldehyde is
questions.solution: In L-glyceraldehyde, when drawn in standard Fischer projection with $-\text{CHO}$ group at top and $-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ group at bottom, the $-\text{OH}$ group is on the left. Option (3) corresponds to L-glyceraldehyde.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Identify the extensive and intensive property?
options: Mass, temperature, heat, volume – Extensive property
Mass, volume, internal energy – Extensive property
Density, temperature, moles, internal energy – Intensive property
questions.solution: Extensive properties depend upon the amount of substance present. Mass, volume, and internal energy all depend on the amount of matter.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Among Group-15 elements, what is the maximum covalency of an element having weakest E–E bond (E = element)
questions.solution: Single bond energies in Group 15: N-N (167 kJ/mol), P-P (201 kJ/mol), As-As (146 kJ/mol), Sb-Sb (121 kJ/mol). Antimony (Sb) has the weakest E-E bond and its maximum covalency is 5.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: What is the relation between $K_{\text{sp}}$ and $S$ of $\text{Zr}_3(\text{PO}_4)_4$
questions.solution:
$\text{Zr}_3(\text{PO}_4)_4 (s) \rightleftharpoons 3\text{Zr}^{4+} (aq) + 4\text{PO}_4^{3-} (aq)$
$K_{\text{sp}} = (3S)^3 (4S)^4 = 27 \times 256 S^7 = 6912 S^7 \implies S = \left(\frac{K_{\text{sp}}}{6912}\right)^{1/7}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Match the column and choose the correct option
(A) $\left(\frac{\partial H}{\partial T}\right)_P$
(B) $\left(\frac{\partial G}{\partial P}\right)_T$
(C) $\left(\frac{\partial U}{\partial T}\right)_V$
(D) $\left(\frac{\partial G}{\partial T}\right)_P$

Column-II:
(P) $C_P$
(Q) $C_V$
(R) $-S$
(S) $V$
questions.solution: $\left(\frac{\partial H}{\partial T}\right)_P = C_P$, $\left(\frac{\partial G}{\partial P}\right)_T = V$, $\left(\frac{\partial U}{\partial T}\right)_V = C_V$, and $\left(\frac{\partial G}{\partial T}\right)_P = -S$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Consider the following statements S-1 and S-2 and choose the correct option.
S-1 : During corrosion pure metal acts as anode and impure metal acts as cathode.
S-2 : Rate of corrosion is more in alkaline medium than in acidic medium.
options: Both S-1 and S-2 are correct
Both S-1 and S-2 are incorrect
S-1 is correct but S-2 is incorrect
S-1 is incorrect but S-2 is correct
questions.solution: During corrosion, pure metal acts as cathode and impure metal spot acts as anode. Acidic medium accelerates corrosion while alkaline medium retards it. Thus both S-1 and S-2 are incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: In Ru and Nb, if in Ru, $4d$ electrons are $x$ and in Nb, $4d$ electrons are $y$ then find the sum of $x$ and $y$.
questions.solution:
$_{44}\text{Ru} \Rightarrow [\text{Kr}] 4d^7 5s^1 \implies x = 7$.
$_{41}\text{Nb} \Rightarrow [\text{Kr}] 4d^4 5s^1 \implies y = 4$.
$x + y = 7 + 4 = 11$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
$\text{Ni}^{2+} + 2\text{DMG} \longrightarrow \text{Complex}$
How many hydrogen bonds are present in a molecule of the complex?
questions.solution: The nickel-dimethylglyoximate complex $[\text{Ni(DMG)}_2]$ contains 2 intramolecular hydrogen bonds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: How many $\text{R–Br}$ can form isopentane on reaction with $\text{Mg/dry ether}$ followed by $\text{H}_2\text{O}$?
questions.solution:
Isopentane is 2-methylbutane. The corresponding alkyl bromides $\text{R-Br}$ are:
1) 1-bromo-2-methylbutane
2) 2-bromo-2-methylbutane
3) 2-bromo-3-methylbutane
4) 1-bromo-3-methylbutane
Total 4 $\text{R-Br}$ compounds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 \xrightarrow{\text{Monobromination}} \text{Single product}$
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 \xrightarrow[4\text{ moles of }\text{H}_2/\text{Cat.}]{\text{Completely hydrogenated product}}$
Find the number of $\pi$-electrons in $\text{C}_6\text{H}_6$.
questions.solution:
Degree of unsaturation of $\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 = 4$.
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6$ is a symmetrical dialkyne (1,5-hexadiyne, $\text{HC}\equiv\text{C-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-C}\equiv\text{CH}$). Total number of $\pi$-bonds $= 4$, so the number of $\pi$-electrons $= 8$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Calculate the radius of first excited state of $\text{He}^+$ ion (in \text{\AA})
questions.solution:
$r = a_0 \frac{n^2}{z}$.
For first excited state of $\text{He}^+$: $n = 2, z = 2$.
$r = a_0 \frac{2^2}{2} = 2 a_0 = 2 \times 0.529\text{ \AA} = 1.058\text{ \AA} \approx 1\text{ \AA}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If $2x^2 + (\cos\theta)x - 1 = 0$, $\theta \in [0, 2\pi]$ has roots $\alpha$ and $\beta$. Then the sum of maximum and minimum value of $\alpha^4 + \beta^4$.
questions.solution:
$\alpha + \beta = \frac{-\cos\theta}{2}$, $\alpha\beta = -\frac{1}{2}$.
$\alpha^2 + \beta^2 = (\alpha+\beta)^2 - 2\alpha\beta = \frac{\cos^2\theta + 4}{4}$.
$\alpha^4 + \beta^4 = (\alpha^2 + \beta^2)^2 - 2\alpha^2\beta^2 = \left(\frac{\cos^2\theta + 4}{4}\right)^2 - \frac{1}{2}$.
For minimum, $\cos\theta = 0 \implies \text{Minimum} = 1 - \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{2}$.
For maximum, $\cos\theta = 1 \implies \text{Maximum} = \frac{25}{16} - \frac{1}{2} = \frac{17}{16}$.
Sum $= \frac{1}{2} + \frac{17}{16} = \frac{25}{16}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If $\theta \in [0, 2\pi]$ satisfying the system of equations $2\sin^2\theta = \cos2\theta$ and $2\cos^2\theta = 3\sin\theta$. Then the sum of all real values of $\theta$ is
questions.solution:
Adding both equations: $2 = 1 - 2\sin^2\theta + 3\sin\theta \implies 2\sin^2\theta - 3\sin\theta + 1 = 0$.
$(2\sin\theta - 1)(\sin\theta - 1) = 0$.
If $\sin\theta = 1$, then $2\sin^2\theta = 2 \neq \cos 2\theta = -1$ (not possible).
So $\sin\theta = \frac{1}{2} \implies \theta = \frac{\pi}{6}, \frac{5\pi}{6}$.
Sum of all values $= \frac{\pi}{6} + \frac{5\pi}{6} = \pi$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let $A = \{1, 2, 3, 4\}$ and $B = \{1, 4, 9, 16\}$. If $f : A \rightarrow B$, number of many-one functions from $A$ to $B$ are
questions.solution:
Total functions $= 4^4 = 256$.
Number of one-one functions $= 4! = 24$.
Number of many-one functions $= 256 - 24 = 232$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: 4 boys and 3 girls are to be seated in a row such that all girls seat together and two particular boys $B_1$ and $B_2$ are not adjacent to each other. Then the number of ways in which this arrangement can be done.
questions.solution:
Grouping 3 girls together as a single block along with remaining 2 boys $B_3, B_4$ gives 3 units, which can be seated in $3! \times 3!$ ways.
This creates 4 spaces into which $B_1$ and $B_2$ can be placed: ${}^4C_2 \times 2!$.
Total ways $= {}^4C_2 \times 2! \times 3! \times 3! = 6 \times 2 \times 6 \times 6 = 432$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If the sum $\sum_{r=0}^{30} \frac{r^2 \left({}^{30}C_r\right)^2}{{}^{30}C_{r-1}} = \alpha \cdot 2^{29}$, then $\alpha$ is equal to

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Consider a function $f(x) = \int_0^{x^2} \frac{t^2 - 8t + 15}{e^t} dt$. The number of points of extrema are
questions.solution:
$f'(x) = \frac{2x(x^4 - 8x^2 + 15)}{e^{x^2}} = \frac{2x(x^2 - 5)(x^2 - 3)}{e^{x^2}}$.
$f'(x) = 0 \implies x = 0, \pm\sqrt{5}, \pm\sqrt{3}$.
Since $f'(x)$ changes sign at each of these 5 points, there are 5 points of extrema.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let $A$ and $B$ are two events such that $P(A \cap B) = \frac{1}{10}$ and $P(A/B)$ and $P(B/A)$ are the roots of the equation $12x^2 - 7x + 1 = 0$, then $\frac{P(\bar{A} \cup \bar{B})}{P(\bar{A} \cap \bar{B})}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Roots of $12x^2 - 7x + 1 = 0$ are $\frac{1}{3}$ and $\frac{1}{4}$.
$P(A/B) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)} \implies P(B) = \frac{1/10}{1/4} = \frac{4}{10}$ (or $\frac{3}{10}$).
$P(B/A) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(A)} \implies P(A) = \frac{1/10}{1/3} = \frac{3}{10}$.
$P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B) = \frac{3}{10} + \frac{4}{10} - \frac{1}{10} = \frac{6}{10}$.
$\frac{P(\bar{A} \cup \bar{B})}{P(\bar{A} \cap \bar{B})} = \frac{1 - P(A \cap B)}{1 - P(A \cup B)} = \frac{1 - 1/10}{1 - 6/10} = \frac{9/10}{4/10} = \frac{9}{4}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Number of terms in an arithmetic progression is $2n$. Sum of terms occurring at even places is 40 and sum of terms occurring at odd places is 55. If the first term exceeds the last term by 27, then $n$ equals to
questions.solution:
Let terms be $a, a+d, \dots, a+(2n-1)d$.
Sum of even terms: $n(a+d) + d \frac{n(n-1)}{2} \cdot 2 = na + n^2d = 40$.
Sum of odd terms: $na + dn(n-1) = 55$.
Subtracting: $dn(n-1) - n^2d = 15 \implies -nd = 15$.
Also $a - (a + (2n-1)d) = 27 \implies -(2n-1)d = 27$.
Dividing the two equations: $\frac{2n-1}{n} = \frac{27}{15} = \frac{9}{5} \implies 10n - 5 = 9n \implies n = 5$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The perpendicular distance of point $P(3, 4, 5)$ from the line $\vec{r} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k} + \lambda(4\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 5\hat{k})$ is
questions.solution:
Any point $A$ on the line is $(2 + 4\lambda, -1 - \lambda, 1 + 5\lambda)$.
$\vec{AP} = (4\lambda - 1)\hat{i} - (\lambda + 5)\hat{j} + (5\lambda - 4)\hat{k}$.
$\vec{AP} \cdot (4\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 5\hat{k}) = 0 \implies 16\lambda - 4 + \lambda + 5 + 25\lambda - 20 = 0 \implies 42\lambda = 19 \implies \lambda = \frac{19}{42}$.
$|AP| = \sqrt{(4\lambda - 1)^2 + (\lambda + 5)^2 + (5\lambda - 4)^2} = \sqrt{\frac{19}{42}}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: In the expansion of $\left(x + \sqrt{x^3-1}\right)^5 + \left(x - \sqrt{x^3-1}\right)^5$, where $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ and $\delta$ are the coefficient of $x, x^3, x^5$ and $x^7$ respectively. If $\alpha u - \beta v = 18$, $\gamma u + \delta v = 20$ then $u + v$ equal to.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let $A(6, 8)$, $B(10\cos\alpha, -10\sin\alpha)$ and $C(-10\sin\alpha, -10\cos\alpha)$ be 3 points and if orthocentre of the triangle $ABC$ is $(0, 9)$ then $100\sin^2\alpha$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Distance of $A, B, C$ from origin is 10, so origin $(0, 0)$ is the circumcentre.
Orthocentre $H = (0, 9)$. Centroid $G$ divides $HO$ in ratio $2:1$.
$x_G = 0 \implies \frac{6 + 10\cos\alpha - 10\sin\alpha}{3} = 0 \implies 15\sin\alpha - 10\cos\alpha = 6$.
$y_G = 3 \implies \frac{8 - 10\sin\alpha - 10\cos\alpha}{3} = 3 \implies 10\sin\alpha + 10\cos\alpha = -1$.
Subtracting gives $20\sin\alpha = 5 \implies 10\sin\alpha = \frac{5}{2}$.
$100\sin^2\alpha = \frac{25}{4}$.

Circle is $(x-3)^2 + y^2 \le 1$. Line through origin with maximum slope is tangent to the circle.
In $\triangle OCP$ (center $C(3,0)$ and radius 1), $\sin\theta = \frac{1}{3} \implies \tan\theta = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A relation $R$ is defined on set $A, A = \{1, 2, 3\}$ and $R = \{(1, 2), (2, 3)\}$. Elements are added such that $R$ becomes reflexive and transitive but not symmetric. Find the number of such relations.
questions.solution:
Reflexive requires adding $(1,1), (2,2), (3,3)$. Transitive requires adding $(1,3)$.
Base relation $R_0 = \{(1,1), (2,2), (3,3), (1,2), (2,3), (1,3)\}$.
Additional pairs available to add are $(2,1), (3,2), (3,1)$.
Checking combinations that preserve non-symmetry:
1) Add $(2,1)$ only
2) Add $(3,2)$ only
3) Add neither
Total 3 such relations are possible.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ be two unit vectors such that angle between $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ is $\frac{\pi}{3}$. If $\lambda\vec{a} + 3\vec{b}$ and $2\vec{a} + \lambda\vec{b}$ are perpendicular to each other, then the product of all possible values of $\lambda$ is ____
questions.solution:
$(\lambda\vec{a} + 3\vec{b}) \cdot (2\vec{a} + \lambda\vec{b}) = 0$
$2\lambda |\vec{a}|^2 + 3\lambda |\vec{b}|^2 + (\lambda^2 + 6)\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} = 0$
Since $|\vec{a}|=|\vec{b}|=1$ and $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} = \cos\frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{1}{2}$:
$5\lambda + (\lambda^2 + 6)\frac{1}{2} = 0 \implies \lambda^2 + 10\lambda + 6 = 0$.
Product of roots $= 6$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Consider two curves $E_1 : \frac{x^2}{a^2} + \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1$ with eccentricity $e_1$ and $E_2 : \frac{x^2}{A^2} + \frac{y^2}{B^2} = 1$ with eccentricity $e_2$. If $\frac{e_1}{e_2} = \frac{1}{3}$ and distance between foci of both curves is $2\sqrt{3}$ and $a - A = 4$, then the sum of lengths of latus rectum of both curves is
questions.solution:
Foci distance $= 2ae_1 = 2Ae_2 = 2\sqrt{3} \implies ae_1 = Ae_2 = \sqrt{3}$.
$\frac{e_1}{e_2} = \frac{A}{a} = \frac{1}{3} \implies a = 3A$.
Since $a - A = 4 \implies A = 2, a = 6$.
$e_1 = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{6}, e_2 = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$.
$b^2 = 36\left(1 - \frac{3}{36}\right) = 33 \implies B^2 = 4\left(1 - \frac{3}{4}\right) = 1$.
Latus rectum of $E_1 = \frac{2b^2}{a} = \frac{66}{6} = 11$.
Latus rectum of $E_2 = \frac{2B^2}{A} = \frac{2}{2} = 1$.
Sum $= 11 + 1 = 12$.

questions.text: Let $P(10, -2, -1)$ and $Q$ be the point of perpendicular drawn from point $R(1, 7, 6)$ on the line joining the points $(2, -5, 11)$ and $(-6, 7, -5)$. Then the length $PQ$ is
questions.solution:
The line $L_1$ joining $(2, -5, 11)$ and $(-6, 7, -5)$ has equation $\frac{x - 2}{2} = \frac{y + 5}{-3} = \frac{z - 11}{4}$.
Any point on $L_1$ is $A(2\lambda + 2, -3\lambda - 5, 4\lambda + 11)$.
$\vec{RA} = (2\lambda + 1)\hat{i} + (-3\lambda - 12)\hat{j} + (4\lambda + 5)\hat{k}$.
Since $RA \perp L_1 \implies 2(2\lambda + 1) - 3(-3\lambda - 12) + 4(4\lambda + 5) = 0 \implies 29\lambda = -58 \implies \lambda = -2$.
Foot of perpendicular $Q = (-2, 1, 3)$.
Length $PQ = \sqrt{(10 + 2)^2 + (-2 - 1)^2 + (-1 - 3)^2} = \sqrt{144 + 9 + 16} = \sqrt{169} = 13$.
